title: Adjustment for location and baseline conditions weakened the groundwater-runoff link in 46 Victorian catchments in 2010-2021
abstract: We tested whether the published spatial link between groundwater and runoff shortfalls adds information beyond location and baseline catchment conditions. We used fixed bore and runoff endpoints for 2010-2021 from a verified SCI publication. In 46 Victorian catchments across 14 cells, the raw rank correlation was 0.49. After adjustment for latitude, longitude, baseline rain, runoff/rain ratio and catchment area, it was 0.14, with a conditional 95% cell bootstrap interval of -0.13 to 0.49. SILO rain gave 0.15 (-0.19 to 0.49). Adding groundwater raised squared error by 395% when geographic cells were held out. A few extreme errors dominate this loss. Deleting any one test cell and two ridge checks did not produce a positive total gain. The all-depth sample retains a positive adjusted association of 0.30 (0.05 to 0.56; 65 catchments). This limits the additional spatial evidence from shallow-bore head shortfalls under the tested models. It does not rule out a groundwater mechanism tied to climate or landscape. The study reuses one observed endpoint set; it is not independent data replication. Few cells, shared bores, source-model error and unmeasured hydraulic gradients limit inference. Code, hashes, aggregate results, all bootstrap draws and a figure are supplied.

display.caption: Raw and adjusted rank links, and held-out geographic-cell error reduction. Bars are conditional 95% cell bootstrap intervals. Negative error reduction means worse prediction. The error axis is symmetric log beyond plus or minus 100%. These are endpoint associations, not causal effects.
